_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis, including primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis and post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 1 (INCB-351), a double-blind, placebo-controlled pivotal trial
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study in 309 patients refractory to or not candidates for available therapy
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with intermediate-2 or high-risk myelofibrosis with palpable splenomegaly at least 5 cm below the costal margin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving >=35% reduction from baseline in spleen volume at Week 24 as measured by MRI or CT
pivotal_trials.result: 35% or greater spleen volume reduction at Week 24: 65 (41.9%) Jakafi vs 1 (0.7%) placebo; P < 0.0001. 50% or greater reduction in Total Symptom Score by Week 24: 68 (45.9%) Jakafi vs 8 (5.3%) placebo; P < 0.0001.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 2 (INCB-352), an open-label, randomized supporting trial
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized study in 219 patients randomized 2:1 to Jakafi versus best available therapy
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with intermediate-2 or high-risk myelofibrosis with palpable splenomegaly at least 5 cm below the costal margin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving 35% or greater reduction from baseline in spleen volume at Week 48 as measured by MRI or CT
pivotal_trials.n: 219 patients (Jakafi N=146, Best Available Therapy N=73)
pivotal_trials.result: 35% or greater spleen volume reduction at Week 48: 41 (28.5%) Jakafi vs 0 best available therapy; P < 0.0001.

key_safety: Most common hematologic adverse reactions (incidence >20%) are thrombocytopenia (34% vs 9% placebo) and anemia (31% vs 14% placebo); most common non-hematologic adverse reactions (>10%) are bruising (23.2%), dizziness (18.1%) and headache (14.8%).
target_moa: Ruxolitinib is a kinase inhibitor that inhibits Janus Associated Kinases JAK1 and JAK2, which mediate signaling of cytokines and growth factors important for hematopoiesis and immune function; myelofibrosis is associated with dysregulated JAK1 and JAK2 signaling.

advisory_committee.vote: No Oncology Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was planned for this submission because the benefits were evident in two adequate and well-controlled trials.

description.text: Added dosing guidance for patients initiating therapy with platelet counts between 50 and 100 x 10^9/L

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the package insert that provide guidance to physicians regarding a JAKAFI® (Ruxolitinib) Tablets starting dose and dosing strategy for patients who initiate therapy with platelet counts between 50 \times 10^9/L and 100 \times 10^9/L.

description.text: Labeling update adding 3-year median follow-up overall survival data and dose titration/modification information (no new indication)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the package insert that include overall survival data based on 3 year median follow-up from the two randomized Phase 3 studies, INCB 18424-351 and INCB 18424-352 (CINC424A2352), and dose titration information based on experience in these 2 studies. In addition, the Dosage and Administration section has been updated to include dose modifications for patients who are on a stable dose of Jakafi® and then start treatment with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor or fluconazole. Lastly, additional text has been added to the Warnings and Precautions Sections 5.2 and 5.3.

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of patients with polycythemia vera who have had an inadequate response to or are intolerant of hydroxyurea

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication for the treatment of patients with polycythemia vera who have had an inadequate response to or are intolerant of hydroxyurea.

description.text: Labeling-only update adding Warnings for hepatitis B reactivation and hyperlipidemia and correcting/updating efficacy results; no new indication or population added

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the Prescribing Information including the addition of a Warning and Precaution for reactivation or worsening of hepatitis B infection to Section 5; the addition of a Warning and Precaution for hyperlipidemia to Section 5; correction of the results of the primary analysis of the primary and secondary endpoints in Section 14; and addition of information regarding durability of responses in Section 14.

description.text: Updated Pediatric Use section to describe ruxolitinib experience in pediatric populations based on Study INCB 18424-269 in children with high-risk acute lymphoblastic leukemia

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the labeling to update the Pediatric Use section of the Prescribing Information to describe the available experience of ruxolitinib in the pediatric populations based on data from Study INCB 18424-269 entitled "A Phase 2 Study of the JAK1/JAK2 Inhibitor Ruxolitinib With Chemotherapy in Children With De Novo High-Risk CRLF2-Rearranged and/or JAK Pathway-Mutant Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia."

orphan_indication.text: Jakafi (ruxolitinib phosphate) was granted Orphan Drug Status for myelofibrosis.

citations.quote: N/A. Jakafi™ (ruxolitinib phosphate) has been granted Orphan Drug Status for myelofibrosis.

summary.text: Ruxolitinib (Jakafi), a new molecular entity and first-in-class JAK1/JAK2 kinase inhibitor, received full approval for intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials; it had been granted Orphan Drug Status for myelofibrosis, and because of the orphan designation the sponsor was exempt from PREA pediatric assessment requirements.

citations.quote: Jakafi™ (ruxolitinib) is a new molecular entity and the first of a new class of kinase inhibitors, that of JAK1 and JAK2 kinases, which act in signaling pathways involved in myeloid cell proliferation.

I recommend that ruxolitinib be granted Full Approval for patients with intermediate-2 and high-risk myelofibrosis, including primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis, and post-essential thrombocytopenia myelofibrosis with the labeling recommended by the review team.
N/A. Jakafi™ (ruxolitinib phosphate) has been granted Orphan Drug Status for myelofibrosis.
Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.
